first_impression.reaction: I searched 'get married in new zealand' because it's the easy option for our older relatives: short flight, no visa. The intro answers the legal question in two lines and admits the paperwork 'won't, quite' look after itself, which I liked. No 'fairytale' or 'dream day'. The licence section is really useful. Where it falls down is the bit we actually have to decide: which region, which months, and roughly what it costs. And it still doesn't tell me how my grandparents get from the airport to a lodge.

journey.quote: New Zealand feels close and familiar, just across the Tasman, and that makes it easy to assume the paperwork will look after itself. It won't, quite.
journey.reaction: That's exactly what I'd assumed. Honest, calm, not trying to sell me a fantasy. Good start.

journey.quote: A registry ceremony suits couples who want the legal marriage done quietly, with the celebration held separately.
journey.reaction: Clear trade-off, plainly said. We'd go personalised, but good to know the option.

journey.quote: For an outdoor wedding, the back-up is your wet-weather plan in legal form, so name it with care.
journey.reaction: This is the insider detail I'd never have known. The licence only covers the venues named on it. Going straight into the planning doc.

journey.quote: Build that appointment into your first days on the ground, well before the rehearsal and the guest welcome.
journey.reaction: Useful, but now I need to know how many days early we have to fly in, and where the registry offices are relative to, say, Queenstown. It says the addresses are on the form, which isn't much help when I'm deciding a region.

journey.section: Before you fly: entry and documents
journey.quote: An Australian driver's licence is not approved ID for buying alcohol or entering licensed premises, so guests heading to a bar after the reception should carry their passport.
journey.reaction: Ha, my cousins would absolutely get caught by this. Small, practical, the kind of thing that makes me trust the rest.

journey.section: When to get married in New Zealand
journey.quote: There is no single right month, and the seasons play out differently from the subtropical north to the alpine south.
journey.reaction: Fair, but then it only describes Queenstown and hands me questions to ask. I came out knowing nothing about which months suit a wedding with older guests.

journey.section: When to get married in New Zealand
journey.quote: Earthquakes are a constant risk, large damaging quakes can happen at any time, and all of New Zealand's coastline is at risk of a tsunami.
journey.reaction: Honest, and in the right section this time, but Mum reads 'tsunami' and 'volcanoes' back to back and starts worrying. One line on what that means in practice for a wedding week would help.

journey.quote: Ask your venue how guests travel in from Auckland for your dates.
journey.reaction: This is our biggest worry and the page just hands it back to us. No airports, no drive times, nothing comparing Queenstown with Waiheke for 80 guests. The regions read like a tourism brochure.

journey.quote: Lodges, vineyard estates and private homes are the usual settings for a New Zealand wedding at this level, and each prices differently.
journey.reaction: So... how much? Not even a range. 'Each prices differently' is the kind of line that makes me think it's expensive and they don't want to say.

journey.quote: **Deposits and contracts:** whose name is on the contract, in which currency are payments made, and when do deposits become non-refundable?
journey.reaction: Exactly the hidden-costs question I'd want to ask. Good.

journey.quote: **Security:** how does your security work, and how would it work alongside a private team we bring?
journey.reaction: A private team we bring? We're not celebrities. Reads like it was written for someone else.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you as one point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: AUD and fee in writing are the right reassurances. 'Start to finish' is what every planner says though. Who's actually there on the day in New Zealand?

journey.section: Plan your New Zealand wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Everything around it is where the planning begins.
journey.reaction: Nice close, no hard sell. Calm enough to send to Mum and Dad.

Will you handle the BDM 58 form, certificate and Apostille for us, or is that on us? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange guest airport transfers, including for grandparents? (deferred business detail)
Are there Wedded Privileges at New Zealand lodges? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: Lodges, vineyard estates and private homes are the usual settings for a New Zealand wedding at this level, and each prices differently.
turn_offs_found.why: Vague pricing with no range. Feeds straight into our hidden-costs fear and makes me suspect the number is scary.

turn_offs_found.quote: **Security:** how does your security work, and how would it work alongside a private team we bring?
turn_offs_found.why: Assumes we travel with private security. Pitched at a celebrity-type client, so the list feels not written for us and a bit showy to share with friends.

turn_offs_found.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you as one point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Start to finish' is the generic end-to-end claim every planner makes; without a New Zealand wedding or a named person on the ground it doesn't answer what it actually means.

would_share_with: James: 'Applying from Australia' and 'Your two witnesses', because the 3-day minimum, 3-month expiry and named back-up venue decide our timing and venue shortlist

My parents: the intro and 'Will our New Zealand marriage be recognised in Australia?', because Dad will ask if it's legal at home. I'd skip the earthquake and volcano paragraph for Mum until I know what it means in practice

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [talk to Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=get-married-in-new-zealand&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: No pressure, and AUD plus fee in writing are right. But we're 14 months out, I don't know which region or month, there's no price range and no real New Zealand wedding to look at. I'd read another post or two first.

top_3_changes: Make 'Choosing your region' help us choose: 'Ask your venue how guests travel in from Auckland for your dates.' hands back our biggest worry. Name the arrival airport and rough transfer for each region so we can picture grandparents getting there.

Give a positive steer on months: 'There is no single right month, and the seasons play out differently from the subtropical north to the alpine south.' leaves us with only questions and hazards. Add a line or two of what each season suits, per region if sourced.
Fix the venues section: replace 'each prices differently' with at least a From AUD range (with sign-off), and drop the 'private team we bring' security framing that doesn't fit couples like us.

open_questions.question: Does the source pack hold airport and transfer details per region, or seasonal guidance beyond Queenstown, to give 'Choosing your region' and 'When to get married' a positive steer?
Is a From AUD venue range available for sign-off, or should the pricing line at least say pricing is not published and how to get it?
Is the private security question in 'Venues and planning' meant for a different persona? It misses for this couple again, as it did on Costa Rica.
